about.title: Apple Valley Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Apple Valley covers a lot of ground, and most of daily life here plays out on property someone else is responsible for maintaining: the businesses along Bear Valley Road and Route 18, apartment walkways, gas station lots, and the parking areas near Apple Valley Road and Kiowa Road. When a wet entryway, cracked pavement, loose mat, or unlit stairwell puts you on the ground, the question under California law is usually notice. Did the owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That question gets answered with evidence, and the evidence disappears fast. Store video gets overwritten. Spills get mopped. Broken tiles get patched. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect people hurt in falls in Apple Valley and elsewhere in San Bernardino County with an independent attorney who handles premises cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You focus on healing; the attorney focuses on the proof.

whyChoose.title: Why Apple Valley Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys Who Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California generally asks the injured person to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys in our network build that case with inspection logs, maintenance records, and witness accounts, not guesswork.

items.title: Fast Action to Preserve Surveillance Video
items.desc: Most Apple Valley businesses keep camera footage for only days or weeks before it is recorded over. Being connected quickly means a preservation demand can go out before that evidence is gone.

items.title: Clear Guidance on Deadlines and Shared Fault
items.desc: You typically have two years to file, but claims involving a public entity move on a much shorter clock. And because California uses pure comparative fault, being partly to blame reduces a recovery rather than eliminating it, which an attorney can explain in plain terms.

items.question: I tripped on a broken sidewalk or in a town park in Apple Valley. Is my deadline different?
items.answer: It very likely is. When the property belongs to a public entity such as the Town of Apple Valley, San Bernardino County, or the State, California requires a formal government claim first, and that window is generally six months rather than two years. Missing it can end the case before it starts, so it is worth speaking with an attorney soon rather than waiting to see how your injuries develop.

items.question: The store says I should have watched where I was walking. Does that mean I have no case?
items.answer: Not under California law. The state follows pure comparative fault, so if a jury decided you were partly responsible, your recovery would be reduced by that percentage instead of wiped out. Whether the hazard was visible, whether warning signs were posted, and how long the condition existed all factor into that analysis, and an attorney can weigh those details for you.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Photograph the exact spot, your footwear, and anything that contributed, and write down the names of anyone who saw it happen. Ask the business for an incident report and request that surveillance video be saved; an attorney connected through LawProactive can send that request formally so it carries weight.
